main_text.p: extat in L.2. non aliter,69.§.1, de legatis lib. III. Alterum exemplum. Lex est: De reo septem testes cognoscant, eaq; sententia fit rata quam plures ex eo numero dixerint. Cum septem iudices cognouissent, duo censuerūt reum exilio multandū: duo alij pecunia, tres reliqui capite puniendum. Petitur ad supplicium ex sententia triū iudicum, & contradicitur. Hæc Gellius lib.IX.cap.XV. Intentio: Duci te ad supplicium ex plurium iudicum sententia oportet. D. Non oportet. Q. An oporteat? R. Quia lex de bipartita tantum sententia, dua-

page.notes: The first line "extat in L.2." is a fragment continuing from the previous page. "De reo septem" is split across the line end as "se" / "ptem" with a large initial "p" and no printed hyphen; I read it as septem, but this is uncertain [?]. The printed "«" marks in the right margin and the handwritten marks in the margins (top right, bottom right) were left out. "dua-" is a word broken at the page end and carries on to the next page; no catchword is printed.
